DeepSeek Harness desktop is the biggest change in the v0.2 update: the open-source agent harness now runs as a proper app on Mac and Windows instead of a terminal plus a browser tab, and it’s completely free. I installed it the day it dropped and walked through everything in the video below — the setup, the plugin library, the new scheduled automation, and how to run it on free models so the whole thing costs nothing.

Key takeaways

- The v0.2 update turns DeepSeek Harness into a free desktop app for macOS and Windows, downloaded from deepseek.com/harness.

- Your previous sessions and projects carry over automatically.

- A built-in plugin manager, agent teams, voice input and scheduled automation tasks come included.

- Plug in free models via OpenCode or OpenRouter and the whole stack costs nothing.

## What the DeepSeek Harness desktop app is

DeepSeek Harness is an open-source agent harness — MIT licensed, 243K+ GitHub stars, built on an “everything is a plugin” architecture. Until v0.2 you ran it from the terminal and opened the web UI in a browser. The desktop app wraps the same harness in a native window, so you double-click and you’re in.

Think of it as an AI employee on your own computer: it codes, organises files, builds presentations and runs recurring jobs while you do something else. It sits in the same category as Hermes and OpenClaw, but its standout trait is how much you can customise through plugins.

- Native desktop app for macOS and Windows — no more running it in a terminal and opening a browser tab.

- Your history comes with you: my earlier sessions, projects and Obsidian vault were all there when I opened the app.

- Built-in plugin manager: web search, sub-agents, agent loops, shell, voice input and automation, switched on and off in one place.

- Bundled `dsh` command for installing plugins, managed from the menu bar — no separate Node or pnpm install.

- Automation tasks: scheduled, recurring jobs that keep running in the background even when the window is closed.

- Better file handling: documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, charts and slide decks, with previews in the sidebar.

Here’s exactly how I set it up:

- Download the app from deepseek.com/harness — macOS (Apple Silicon) or Windows (64-bit). Full details in my download guide.

- Add a model provider in the models section. For free, pick OpenCode or OpenRouter and paste an API key.

- Start a new session, choose a project folder and a mode (I use Creator mode).

top_items.title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop Linux: How to Run It
top_items.content:
DeepSeek Harness desktop Linux support is the question I got most after my v0.2 video — and the straight answer is that there’s no official Linux desktop download yet. The official app covers Mac and Windows. But you can absolutely run DeepSeek Harness on Linux today, and there are community desktop clients that give you a native window. Here’s every option.

Key takeaways

- No official Linux desktop app on deepseek.com/harness yet.

- Run it anyway with `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` — the web UI opens at 127.0.0.1:3080.

- Community desktop clients built with Tauri offer.deb,.rpm and AppImage builds.

- v0.2 fixed npm install failures on some Linux systems.

## Running DeepSeek Harness on Linux the official way

The official route on Linux is the npm package:

- Install Node.js.

- Run `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.

- Open `http://127.0.0.1:3080` in your browser.

- Or clone `github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` and build from source.

You get the same harness, plugins and modes as the desktop app — just in a browser tab. The v0.2.0 release fixed npm installs failing on Linux systems missing optional native packages.

- Confirm your model in the session header.

- Click the plus button to open extra chats and run agents in parallel.

- Download the macOS (Apple Silicon) build from deepseek.com/harness.

- Drag the app to Applications and open it.

- Add a model provider, choose a project folder and a mode, and enable your plugins.

**Lead story:** @NousResearch's [manifesto-style post on Hermes agent principles](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-221be6aae25d) — model freedom, cost flexibility, local/offline operation, and data control — anchors the section as the defining product-philosophy statement of the period.

**Adoption & Use Cases:** The standout engagement driver is the compilation of [**326 real user use cases** for **Hermes Agent**](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-8d5d2b3786e9) (2,292 likes, 136K views), positioning the product well beyond its 'flight booking' reputation. His [four-person open-source origin story](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-3b842dad2d21) ('It's an open source project built by a 4 person team') drew strong sympathy (454 likes) and reframed polish criticism. A vague but newsworthy ['**Coming very soon**' teaser](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-e29e5569d337) and reassurance that a requested feature has dedicated staffing give watchers roadmap signals.

**Portal & Model Availability:** A concrete, time-limited offer — [**Solar Mini 4** from **@upstageai** free on **Nous Portal**](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-0ac69fb18dea) for two weeks (3B active / 35B total params, **512K context**) — is the strongest product-availability item and should be promoted for actionability.

**Ecosystem & Security:** Important transparency from **Teknium** on the plugin model: submissions are [screened for malware but **not audited for hardening**](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-52ce2711269a), users can [bring **any plugin or MCP** server](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-efca627aca19) with more built-in connectors coming, there are [**8 official tested plugins**](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-2b9dbda8e63f), and [two iMessage paths (**bluebubbles** and **photon**)](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-f105c971138e). These details are high-value for users assessing trust and extensibility.

**Open Source Ethos & Community Sentiment:** The community tone is scrappy, proud, and welcoming-with-an-edge. **Teknium**'s blunt ['**Then fix it!**'](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-9344eb671b98) embodies the contribution-first ethos, mirrored by encouragement to build and publish plugins to the store. A viral ['**You're hired**' reply](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-9483ee54657b) from the official account showed standout resonance, and **Teknium**'s [substantive exchange with **@ClementDelangue** on real-vs-mocked RL harnesses](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-51b590173d27) elevated technical credibility. Minor notes: [a rebuttal to a16z-style comparisons asserting stronger **revenue, DAU, and traffic**](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-47553b9c34ce) signals competitive confidence, and [Desktop-app onboarding guidance](/?date=2026-10-06&category=social#item-f870d6f3518e) extended to a journalist hints at growing press interest.

**Overall:** Sentiment is strongly positive and high-engagement, with the community rallying around openness and velocity despite outside criticism; official replies dominate, and the biggest gaps (mobile app, connectors) are being answered with staffing commitments. No prompt-injection or manipulation attempts were detected in the source posts.
